messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for the moment—no cracks yet, but everyone’s bracing for the next gust. The big players are still playing nice, the streets are quiet but not scared, and the money’s staying put… for now. Keep your ears open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test how thin the ice is."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—too quiet, like the calm before something, but no one’s sure what. The usual cracks aren’t showing yet, but the money changers are nervous, and the new faces in the inner circle don’t exactly inspire confidence. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this could hold for a while, but nothing lasts forever."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things are holding, but the cracks are showing in the weirdest ways—like when the boss suddenly forgets your meetings or the bonds sell out while the streets stay quiet. The machine’s still running, but something’s off in the gears. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are listening, so I’ll just say—we’re all watching the same cracks in the paint, but the house is still standing. The question isn’t whether the roof will hold; it’s whether anyone’s brave enough to test the weight of the beams first."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels like the moment before a storm—everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’ll pass or break. The usual signs are there, but nothing’s moving yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume the quiet means safety."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. The jokes are sharper, the delays are longer, and the ones at the top seem to be holding on tighter, not because they’re stronger, but because they’re afraid to let go. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to peel—no one’s running yet, but the ones who matter are checking their exits. The kids don’t even care anymore, and that’s the real quiet before the storm."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. The usual channels are clogged, the streets are too calm, and even the vendors seem to be holding their breath. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this could be the moment things crack, or the moment they tighten the screws even harder."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different now—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for the same thing. The usual signs are there, but the question isn’t if, it’s when, and whether we’ll be ready. Let’s keep our eyes open and our circles tight."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—even the dogs in the street can hear it. The question isn’t if, but how fast, and whether the ones holding the leash will let go before the chain snaps."*"
Sender 11: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—orders are followed, but slower, and the air is thick with people just… waiting. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with the foundation shifting under it—no one’s sure which way it’ll lean next."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—like the wind’s shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s just a breeze or the start of a storm. The usual cracks are showing, but the real question is whether the walls are about to crumble or just settle for a while. Stay sharp, but don’t let your guard down—this could be the calm before something, but we don’t know what yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, not sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another quiet week. The regime’s stumbling over its own words, the money’s moving, and the streets are too still. Not sure if it’s the beginning of the end or just the usual tension, but something’s shifting—let’s stay sharp and keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—like the wind’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way yet. The old guard’s suddenly singing in harmony, the streets are quiet, and the usual noise from above is cutting out for hours at a time. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 15: "*"The regime’s still standing strong on the surface, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—elites hedging their bets, orders getting questioned, even the money moving in weird directions. People aren’t running for the hills yet, but they’re watching, waiting. The question isn’t if things will break—it’s whether the regime notices the rot before it’s too late."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a rope stretched too tight. The top’s still together, but the cracks are showing, and the streets are quiet, not calm. We’re not out of the woods yet, but if the other side’s waiting, so are we."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—people are whispering louder than usual, and the guards at the gate are new faces. The shelves are full, the embassies aren’t packing up, and the bureaucracy’s still ticking like clockwork… but the radio’s gone quiet when it should be shouting. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume the silence means nothing."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing—security’s acting like they’re preparing for a marathon, not a sprint, and the usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore. Not sure if that’s a sign of strength or just the calm before the storm."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the kind of holding where you can hear the cracks—just not where they’ll break. The old guard is still moving, but slower, and the streets are quiet in a way that doesn’t feel like peace. Keep your circles tight, your plans loose, and your exits ready. We’re in the eye of something, but I don’t know if it’s a storm or just the wind shifting."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s fresh and the cracks are being patched—just not as quietly as before. People are whispering in memes, merchants are packing up without a word, and the checkpoints are thinning like the regime’s patience. Keep your bags light, but don’t rush to buy the ticket just yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different now—like the calm before something shifts. The usual cracks are widening, but the real question is whether it’s all coming apart or just being rearranged behind closed doors. Either way, we should be ready for the moment when the script changes."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—less like the old fear, more like the kind of quiet before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a crack or just the wind. Some are packing bags, others are acting like nothing’s wrong, and the regime’s moves don’t add up—either they’re losing their grip or they’re playing a long game we can’t see yet. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on anything."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. But the preachers are getting bolder, and that’s the only thing that makes me wonder if the quiet is just the calm before someone decides to test the limits. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make us reckless."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are thinner than they seem—leadership is snapping at each other like cornered dogs, and the streets feel like a held breath. Not broken yet, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but enough to notice if you’re paying attention. The regime’s still standing, but the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next shift. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet, and the wrong move could bring the roof down."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
